tldr: Canada's Real-Time Rail went live, and Wealthsimple and KOHO were quick to announce support, which puts instant payments on Simplii's roadmap now. Elsewhere, fintechs are shipping practical features (Venmo receipt-splitting, Wise interest and stocks) while banks and exchanges push stablecoins and tokenization.
themes: Fintechs adding savings yield and investing
Stablecoin and tokenization push by banks and exchanges
Generative AI assistants in bank apps

highlights.headline: Canada's Real-Time Rail launched, with Wealthsimple and KOHO announcing participation and KOHO promoting instant payments to millions
highlights.why: Direct competitor Wealthsimple and challenger KOHO are already marketing instant payments, so Simplii needs a clear RTR timeline and customer messaging to avoid looking behind.

highlights.headline: Wise adds Wise Interest and Stocks for US customers
highlights.why: A payments-first fintech is turning into a spend, save and invest hub to keep deposits. This is the same all-in-one model Wealthsimple uses in Canada, so it raises expectations for bundled yield and investing.

highlights.headline: Venmo launches in-app receipt scanning to split bills by item
highlights.why: This sets a new bar for peer-to-peer UX beyond simple transfers. With RTR live, Simplii could pair instant Interac-style transfers with smarter splitting and request flows.

highlights.headline: PNC launches Coinbase-powered stablecoin payments for corporate clients, and NYSE plans to settle tokenized stocks on Avalanche
highlights.why: Large banks and exchanges are moving stablecoins and tokenized assets into mainstream infrastructure. This is an early signal for Simplii to monitor, though it is not yet a retail demand driver.
